items.name: d2r-mobile
items.description: Open-source iOS / macOS compatibility layer for Diablo II: Resurrected with the Reign of the Warlock expansion. Runs your own Switch copy natively on iPhone, iPad and Mac — full touch controls, 60 fps, new endgame modes. Bring your own game files. 开源的《暗黑破坏神 II：狱火重生》术士君临 iOS / macOS 兼容层
items.readme:
# D2R Mobile **An open-source iOS compatibility layer for Diablo II: Resurrected with the Reign of the Warlock expansion.** It brings the Nintendo Switch release you bought, expansion included, to iPhone and iPad in full: the original game code runs natively, every control is rebuilt for touch, the frame rate holds at 60 fps, and you are in a game one second after the main menu. This is not a tech demo that "sort of runs". It is a mobile version polished for daily play, from your first character all the way through the endgame. Platforms: iPhone / iPad (iOS 26 and later) · Game version: Switch release with Reign of the Warlock, 3.3.94012 · English / 中文 · License: MIT · **Bring your own game files** 中文: [README.zh-CN.md](README.zh-CN.md)

| 100% | 60 fps | about 1 s | about 3.8 W | |:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | The original gameplay, because it is the original program | Steady, with no drops once the device warms up | From the main menu into a game | Whole-device power draw at 60 fps | ## What it is, and what it is not **It is:** - The game's own aarch64 program, **executing directly on the device**, with no emulated CPU. iPhone and Switch use the same class of processor; only the handful of instructions that cannot run unchanged under Apple's kernel are rewritten, and every other byte of the program is left exactly as shipped. Every class, every Runeword, Terror Zones, bosses, drop rules and quest flow are identical to the original. - The platform services the game expects — system calls, the file system, the graphics API, audio, input — provided by a small host written for Apple platforms. The graphics API is reimplemented entirely on Apple's Metal with no emulation layer in between, and the shaders are translated offline from the game's originals. - A port built for phones, and taken all the way: a complete touch control scheme, edge-to-edge iPhone and true full-screen iPad display, controller support, a power saver mode, save sync, English and Chinese, and a whole set of endgame modes and quality-of-life features the original never had. **It is not:** - An emulator, cloud gaming, or streaming. - **A source of game content. It contains none and distributes none.** There is no game program, art, text, data table or shader in this repository; all of that is generated on your own machine from your own files (see [docs/GAME_FILES.md](docs/GAME_FILES.md)). What the repository does carry is the interface information we recorded to make the port work — shader interface descriptions, the graphics API function table, addresses inside the program and the like — listed item by item in [docs/DERIVED.md](docs/DERIVED.md). - Online. There is no multiplayer; the game runs fully offline and needs no online account. ## Battle-tested All **44** iPhones and iPads in the closed beta — 35 devices registered for direct install (25 iPhones and 10 iPads), plus 9 TestFlight accounts with one device each — **completed Normal, Nightmare and Hell with multiple characters**, and the experience was excellent. From an iPhone 14 Pro Max with 6 GB of memory to the latest iPad Pro, not one device fell behind. | | Models | |---|---| | iPhone | 14 Pro Max, 15, 15 Pro, 15 Pro Max, 16 Plus, 16 Pro, 16 Pro Max, 17 Pro Max and more | | iPad | iPad Air, iPad mini, iPad Pro 11-inch and 12.9 / 13-inch (including M2 and M4) and more | | Lowest model tested | **iPhone 14 Pro Max (A16, 6 GB): a flawless 60 fps** | iPhone and iPad share a single install package.

## Fast, smooth, and easy on the battery Measured on a real device (iPhone 17 Pro Max): | Item | Reading | |---|---| | In-game frame rate | **60 fps**, steady, with no drops once the device warms up | | App launch | 0.15 s | | To the main menu | about 1 s | | From the main menu into a game | **about 1 s** | | Quick Restart, back in a game | about 1.2 s | | Longest frame when changing acts | about 0.1 s | | Whole-device power, 60 fps | **about 3.8 W** (in camp, 50% brightness): nearly 5 hours of continuous play on a full charge | | Whole-device power, power saver mode at 30 fps | **about 1.85 W**, about half the 60 fps figure, for about twice the battery life | Measurement conditions: power is whole-device power measured on 2026-10-10 on an iPhone 17 Pro Max, standing in the Act I camp at 50% brightness, with 60 fps and power saver mode measured in the same scene; battery life is calculated from the measured power and the battery capacity, not by playing from full to empty. Launch and game-entry times were measured on the same model in 2026-10; frame rate and act-change readings were taken on the same model on 2026-10-12 while moving through areas and changing acts after entering a game. The install package is only a little over 100 MB. The game resources (about 5.6 GB) are placed on the phone separately, and updating the app touches neither your saves nor the resources. Why it is this fast: the program executes natively, and not a single instruction goes through emulation; graphics go straight to Metal; every shader is translated offline and compiled ahead of time, so nothing is compiled when you enter a new scene. Older chips such as the A16 do not support the game's original compressed texture format, so we built a supplementary texture pack for them, and they run at full frame rate too. ## Redesigned for fingers This is not a gamepad pasted onto the screen. Every panel and every action was rebuilt for fingers under one design principle: **keep the original interface language, and use gestures instead of adding buttons to the screen**. Text sizes and tap targets are sized for fingers. You know how to play the moment you pick it up, and it stays comfortable over long sessions.

- **Move**: a virtual stick with precise diagonals; tap an NPC or the ground to path there automatically; doors, portals and cave entrances are tappable across their whole surface. - **Fight**: press a skill button to cast, hold to keep casting, **drag to aim at any angle**; nearby monsters are targeted automatically. Two skill sets. Skills on your secondary weapons cast with one tap — the game swaps weapons, casts, and swaps back — and the button shows the charges remaining. - **Boss health bar**: pinned to the top of the screen, showing the percentage remaining. - **Items**: tap, double-tap, long-press and drag and drop all track your finger. Double-tap gear to equip or unequip it; drag an item anywhere onto the vendor panel to sell it; on a stack, double-tap takes 1 and long-press takes 3; long-press an empty inventory slot to sort everything. - **Text**: typed with the system keyboard. Character names can be in Chinese; leave the name blank for a random one. - **Screen**: on iPhone the 19.5:9 display is filled edge to edge, clear of the notch and rounded corners; on iPad the game fills the entire screen, and the interface centers itself when you open a panel; the 3D picture can be brightened. ### Controller Connect a controller and press any button: the interface switches to the original controller layout, with button prompts at the bottom of every panel. Touch the screen and you are back in the touch interface instantly. Inventory, stash, skill tree, Chronicle and settings are fully controller-navigable, with the same button mapping as on Switch.

## New ways to play, on top of the original Finishing the original game is only the beginning. Without touching the original rules, we added a full set of endgame content that keeps you farming. ### Greater Rift Enter through the red portal in Harrogath after completing Hell. There are 100 levels, and the monsters grow stronger with each one; fill the progress bar and slay the Rift Guardian within 15 minutes to clear a level. Every 2 levels cleared grants +1 Skill Point and +5 Stat Points, and the skill level cap rises from 20 to 40. Every 10 levels has a first-clear reward, and clearing level 10 unlocks six new equipment slots for your mercenary.

### Endgame Boss Rush, Elysium mode, and the Kill Board - **Endgame Boss Rush**: unlocks after completing Hell, with 12 stages; stage 11 is Diablo Clone, and stage 12 is the three Uber bosses. - **Elysium mode** (chosen at character creation): Unique ×5, Set ×3, Runes ×5; the "no drop" chance is cut to a tenth, and bosses always drop as on a first kill. - **Kill Board**: for every boss, the number of kills, the time of the first kill, how many Unique and Set items it has dropped, and your best and average kill times.

### Storage: a collector's paradise - **Chronicle stash**: every identified Unique and Set item has its own fixed slot, shared by all characters, searchable, with deposit and withdraw; the Deposit button sends the Unique and Set items in your inventory and Horadric Cube there in one tap. - **Stash**: widened to 14 columns, with 5 personal pages and 5 shared pages. - **Trove**: the gem, rune and material pages merged into one, with the Horadric Cube's crafting grid in the middle, so finding things and crafting no longer means flipping between pages. Runes, gems and materials you put into the personal or shared pages are filed here automatically. - **Pouch**: an extended inventory. Runes and gems found in the field go into it automatically and take up no inventory space.

### Effortless farming | | | |---|---| | Auto-recast buffs | Buff skills you have learned do not need a slot on the skill bar: when a buff runs out, it is recast the moment you stand still; buffs that come from your secondary weapons (such as Battle Orders from Call to Arms) swap weapons, recast and swap back on their own | | Potions and belt | Auto-drink has two tiers: a healing potion below 50% Life, a rejuvenation potion below 30%; **your mercenary is fed automatically by the same rule**. Potions on the ground are picked up automatically when the belt has room; double-tap an empty belt slot to refill the whole belt | | Loot filter | From Nightmare on, the original loot filter is switched on automatically to hide clutter: light filtering in Nightmare, heavy in Hell | | Auto-pickup | Low runes and gems go straight into the Pouch; the high ones are left for you to pick up yourself | | Valuable drop alerts | High runes and Unique items raise a light beam and land with a different drop sound; the phone vibrates at one of three strengths — light, medium or heavy — according to value | | Runeword helper | Long-press a socketed base to list the Runewords it can make and their stats; once you have the runes, socket them all in one tap | | Minimap guidance | Every map marks its Waypoint and exits; every quest goal is on the map; when a target is off screen, its name is written along the screen edge | | Chores removed | Free identification, free Town Portal with no scrolls needed, spawning right beside the Waypoint, Quick Restart, refreshable vendor stock | | Saves | Saved immediately when you switch apps, swipe the app away or quit; iCloud sync across devices (requires signing with a paid developer account) | Most features can be toggled one by one in game under Options → Custom.

### English and Chinese The whole game switches between English and Chinese under Options → Custom; after a restart, both the interface and the voice acting are in the language you chose. In English, items, skills and monsters use the original Diablo II wording, and everything we added — Greater Rift, Chronicle, the settings page, controller prompts — is in English too.

## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR G["Your game files
(program + resources)"] --> P["Rewriter
changes only a few instructions"] G --> S["Shader translation
original → Metal"] P --> H["Host
system services"] S --> X["Graphics layer
the graphics API on Metal"] H --> A["iOS app
touch and interface"] X --> A ``` | Part | Where | What it does | |---|---|---| | Program rewriter | `dm/tools/patch_nso.py` | Rewrites only the few instructions that cannot run unchanged under Apple's kernel (thread-pointer registers, system calls, timers) and leaves the rest of the program byte-for-byte as shipped | | Host | `dm/host` | Loads the rewritten program and provides the platform services it calls | | Graphics | `dm/gfx` | Implements the game's graphics API on Metal; shaders are translated offline from the game's originals | | iOS app | `dm/ios` | The app shell, touch controls and interface | | Verification | `dm/verify` | Checks that the rewritten code behaves exactly like the original, plus the regression gates every change goes through | **Why you can trust it:** the stability is not luck. The test and verification tooling is part of the project — unit tests for the host and graphics layers, an equivalence check for every rewritten instruction, scripted walkthrough regression for the touch interface, and on-device smoke tests. Start with `make -C dm/host/tests run`, `make -C dm/gfx/tests run` and `dm/verify/regress.sh` (run them inside the Python environment prepared in step 2 below; `regress.sh` also needs `brew install llvm`). How to contribute is in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Getting started Both routes start with **the files of the game you bought**: the Switch release of Diablo II: Resurrected plus the Reign of the Warlock expansion, updated to 3.3.94012. This project is built for the version with that expansion; using it without the expansion is not supported and has not been verified. How to prepare them is in [docs/GAME_FILES.md](docs/GAME_FILES.md). | | With a Mac | Without a Mac | |---|---|---| | Computer | An Apple silicon Mac with Xcode installed | Windows / Linux / a Mac without Xcode | | Method | A full build from source | Download a "shell" with no game content, use the packaging tool to add your own game content, then install it with a sideloading tool | | Status | The main route; everything above comes from it | Works end to end on Windows, from making the package to playing on a device, and the game program produced on the two systems is byte-for-byte identical; the one step nobody has tried yet is signing with a sideloading tool — try it and tell us | | Instructions | The three steps below | [docs/NO_XCODE.md](docs/NO_XCODE.md) | The Apple account used for signing: a paid developer account gives you everything; a free Apple ID works too (no iCloud save sync, and the app has to be re-signed and reinstalled every 7 days). The full list of dependencies is in [docs/DEPENDENCIES.md](docs/DEPENDENCIES.md). ### With a Mac: three steps 1. Put your game files in the workspace (default `~/dm-work`, or set `DM_ROOT`): ``` ~/dm-work/data/switch/3.3.94012/Update/ExeFS/ main, sdk, subsdk0 ~/dm-work/data/switch/3.3.94012/Update/RomFS/ data/… ``` 2. Prepare the workspace. This checks your tools, rewrites the game program, and translates the game's shaders to Metal. The first run takes a while; later runs skip what is already done. ``` ./setup.sh source ~/dm-work/build/cache/dm/venv/bin/activate # run everything after this inside the Python environment setup prepared; if you changed DM_ROOT, use it in place of ~/dm-work ``` 3. Fill in your signing details and build the app: ``` cp dm/ios/local.env.example dm/ios/local.env # set DM_TEAM_ID and DM_BUNDLE_ID; with a free Apple ID also set DM_FREE_ACCOUNT=1 and DM_IOS_UDID, and keep the phone connected while building cd dm/ios && ./run.sh build # targets both iPhone and iPad by default; for iPhone only: DM_DEVICE_FAMILY=1 ./run.sh build ``` The first time you open the app on your phone, it asks for the "game resource folder" — the 18 resource archives from your game files. Where to put them is in the section "The "game resource folder" that goes on the phone" of [docs/GAME_FILES.md](docs/GAME_FILES.md). `./setup.sh check` is a health check: it reports the state of this computer, the tools, the game files and the signing configuration item by item, and for everything missing it says where to get it and which command to run next; it changes nothing. If what you have is a whole game package (`.xci` / `.nsp`), `./setup.sh ` first extracts the game files into place and then carries on (install hactool first). Run `./setup.sh` again after every update to a new commit: it rebuilds the patched binaries and the shader library for the current sources (steps that are already up to date are skipped). It also rewrites three files in the repository that change with your local tool fingerprints (`dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_chain.lock`, `dm/gfx/nvn/dmsh_chain.h`, `dm/gfx/nvn/c1_full.tsv`); that is expected, do not commit them. ### Without a Mac: the shell plus the packaging tool Download our prebuilt "shell" package (`D2RMobile-shell.ipa`), which contains no game content, from this repository's [Releases page](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile/releases), add your own game files, make the install package on Windows or Linux, then sign and install it with a sideloading tool. On this route only, because the computer making the package has no Apple shader compiler, the **first launch** on the phone spends about 7 minutes compiling shaders (once, with a progress bar); a package built with Xcode has no such step. The steps, and how far each one has been verified, are in [docs/NO_XCODE.md](docs/NO_XCODE.md). ## Known limitations | Item | Status | |---|---| | Online play | Out of scope; fully offline | | Game packages in `.nsp` format | Not verified (only `.xci` was tested) | | Signing and installing with a sideloading tool (Sideloadly, AltStore and the like) | Not verified; open an issue and tell us how it went | | Making the package on Linux | Not verified (verified on Windows and Mac) | | The "one-line verdict" and "legacy Chinese name" entries in item notes | These two content tables are not shipped with the repository; you can supply your own, see `dm/ios/tools/annot/README.md` | ## Contributing and feedback - If you hit a problem, open an issue (there is a template); attaching the file exported by Share Diagnostics in the pause menu helps the most. - For the items marked not verified, tell us whether they worked or not. Either answer is valuable. - To change the code: get the test entry points above passing first. Every change has to pass the regression gates. **Taking it to other platforms:** this approach is not limited to iPhone and iPad. It ports directly to Apple silicon Macs — our daily regression tests run the very same package on a Mac. Android phones use the same class of processor, so the game program executes natively there as well, and the route is fully open: the only parts to replace are the sides of the host and the graphics layer that face the platform. The author has no Android phone at hand, and would love to see someone bring it to Android. ## Documentation by part | Document | Covers | |---|---| | [dm/README.md](dm/README.md) | How the whole thing works, directory layout, common commands, the host's source files | | [dm/gfx/README.md](dm/gfx/README.md) | The graphics layer and the shader translation chain | | [dm/ios/README.md](dm/ios/README.md) | The iOS shell, building and smoke testing | | [dm/verify/README.md](dm/verify/README.md) | What each verification tool checks and what it needs | | [docs/GAME_FILES.md](docs/GAME_FILES.md) | Game files: which ones you need, how to get them from your own console, where to put them | | [docs/DEPENDENCIES.md](docs/DEPENDENCIES.md) | Dependencies and third-party licenses | | [docs/NO_XCODE.md](docs/NO_XCODE.md) | Building without Xcode and without a Mac | | [docs/DERIVED.md](docs/DERIVED.md) | Game-related material in this repository: what is here, what is not, and why | ## Legal **You must own the game, including the Reign of the Warlock expansion.** This is an independent, non-commercial project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Blizzard Entertainment or Nintendo. Diablo and Blizzard Entertainment are trademarks of Blizzard Entertainment, Inc.; Nintendo Switch is a trademark of Nintendo. Use it only with a copy of the game that you own. ## License MIT, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Third-party code keeps its own license in its own directory; see [docs/DEPENDENCIES.md](docs/DEPENDENCIES.md).

items.readme: # qwen21-nsfw-pose [![Package checks](https://github.com/Arekejoker/qwen21-nsfw-pose-skill/actions/workflows/validate.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/Arekejoker/qwen21-nsfw-pose-skill/actions/workflows/validate.yml) **Qwen-Image 2.1 本地 NSFW / 姿势出图完整配方** — 作者级提示词结构 + NSFW LoRA + 136 个 3D 姿势库 + VNCCS 人偶精确姿势控制。 基于 ComfyUI + `qwen_image_2.1_int8_convrot` 底模（与 Civitai 作者同款底模），复刻并验证过 Civitai 作者样图（2026-10-12）。 - 适用：Claude Code / Codex / Cursor / OpenClaw（agent 技能）+ 人类手动使用 - 内容：可跟跑的作者案例、强制配方、姿势大胆度阶梯（L0–L3）、完整依赖与安装指南 --- ## 效果展示 ### 本配方输出：同一海边场景的三级对照（L0 → L1 → L2） | L0 · 全着装，无 LoRA（提示词即全部） | L1 · 湿身泳装 + LoRA@1.0 | L2 · 极低机位 + 湿身蹲姿 + LoRA@1.0 | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | 三张图同场景递进：L0 只有提示词；L1 加 LoRA + 显式皮肤/水珠描写；L2 再加低机位与开合姿态。**LoRA 负责质感，提示词负责信息密度，机位负责大胆度。** ### NSFW 效果（⚠️ 以下图片包含裸露内容） **作者原图**（Civitai showcase，本配方复刻的目标）： | 作者 · 淋浴（tawsLoRa） | 作者 · 按摩（tawsLoRa） | 作者 · 自拍（TheseAlpacas） | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | 用 §「快速开始」的命令可复刻淋浴那张（复刻输出已验证与作者原图同场景同构图，见 `downloads/samples/phase5_meta.json` 与本文快速开始一节）。 ### 3D 人偶精确姿势（Route ④，136 姿势库） 默认人物图 `references/src_standing.png`；姿势 = 骨骼旋转 JSON（MakeHuman 网格 + three.js 渲染）， 换姿势且保身份。姿势库来源：HuggingFace 4 个公开仓库（`Totemistyk/General_Poses`、 `Totemistyk/Ballet_PoseStudio`、`MIUProject/VNCCS_PoseLibrary_Main`、 `MIUProject/MySuperPoseRepo`）+ 55 个手工精选，共 **136 个**。 --- ## 快速开始（作者案例跟跑） 前置安装见 [install/setup.md](install/setup.md)。装好后一条命令复刻作者淋浴样图（~5 分钟）： ```bash python3 scripts/qwen_pose_test.py \ --mode t2i --name author_case_shower \ --prompt "$(cat prompts/taws_v13_shower.txt)" \ --seed 80964 \ --steps 50 --cfg 2.5 --sampler er_sde --scheduler beta \ --width 1152 --height 1728 \ --lora "qwen2_1-femaledVaginus-nsfw-v1_3-fine_L22-31.safetensors" \ --lora-strength 1.0 \ --out outputs/author_case/shower.png ``` 对比对象：`downloads/samples/taws_v13_shower_author.jpg`。 完整元数据（提示词/参数/seed/完整工作流）：`downloads/samples/phase5_meta.json`。 ## 三条路线 | 需求 | 路线 | 命令 | | --- | --- | --- | | 新 NSFW/性感图（文字出图） | ① T2I + NSFW LoRA（必开） | `scripts/qwen_pose_test.py --mode t2i` | | 已有角色图换姿势（保脸/保服装） | ② Edit | `scripts/qwen_pose_test.py --mode edit` | | 指定 3D 姿势库里的精确姿势 | ④ VNCCS PoseStudio | `scripts/run_vnccs_ui.py --pose ` | 姿势怎么选（大胆度阶梯 L0–L3、用户要求→姿势族映射表）：见 `SKILL.md` §4，或 `scripts/run_vnccs_ui.py --list-poses` 列出全部 136 个姿势。 ## 配方要点（摘要） - `er_sde` + `beta`，CFG 2.5，50 步，1152×1728 竖版 - **NSFW LoRA 永远开**（默认 `femaledVaginus v1.3b` @ 1.0） - 提示词必须按作者结构写满 7 要素、300–1500 字符、含 LoRA 触发词 - 弱化配方（无 LoRA/短提示词/减步数）前必须告知用户代价，不许默默减弱 完整规则与证据：`SKILL.md`。 ## 目录结构 ``` ├── SKILL.md # agent 技能（完整规则） ├── install/setup.md # 安装指南（模型/LoRA/节点/姿势库） ├── scripts/ # 出图脚本、案例脚本、media_lock.py、validate_package.py ├── workflows/ # qwen21_t2i.json / qwen21_edit.json / VNCCS_PoseStudio_QI2.1.json ├── prompts/ # 3 篇作者原提示词 + 参数 ├── references/ # 效果展示图（L0/L1/L2 海边对照）+ 默认人物图 ├── downloads/samples/ # 作者原图 + 作者元数据 + 原始工作流 JSON └── pose_library/ # 55 个手工精选姿势（安装时拷入 ComfyUI） ``` ## 说明 - 底模与 LoRA 版权归原作者所有（HF `Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1`、Civitai 2986844 / 2958918 / 2988215） - NSFW 示例图仅供配方演示；仓库为公开仓库，介意图片的先收藏后阅读

items.readme:
The world’s software. Rebuilt, open-sourced, and MIT-licensed.

The Everything Project is an effort to rebuild and open-source the world’s software from scratch. From Office to Slack and Photoshop to AutoCAD, we are recreating free, open-source alternatives to all proprietary software. This is a mono-repository containing all the applications and tools developed under the project. [Office](#office) · [Collaboration](#collaboration) · [Creative Tools](#creative-tools) · [Engineering](#engineering) · [Productivity](#productivity) · [Finance](#finance) · [Business](#business) · [Developer Tools](#developer-tools) · [Games](#games)
## Getting started ```sh git clone https://github.com/HeyPuter/everything.git cd everything/src/[app-name] npm install npm run dev ```

items.description: A design system for AI applications. Material, physical, tactile, technical.
items.readme:
# Solid Glass
[The style](#the-style) · [Install](#install) · [What is here](#what-is-here) · [Contributing](#contributing) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/deeplethe/solid-glass?style=flat-square&label=STARS&labelColor=161B22&color=FFC220&logo=github&logoColor=FFFFFF)](https://github.com/deeplethe/solid-glass/stargazers) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/LICENSE-MIT-3FB950?style=flat-square&labelColor=161B22)](LICENSE) [![For AI applications](https://img.shields.io/badge/DESIGNED%20FOR-AI%20APPLICATIONS-8957E5?style=flat-square&labelColor=161B22)](https://deeplethe.github.io/solid-glass/docs/components/status-glyph) [![shadcn/ui](https://img.shields.io/badge/BUILT%20ON-SHADCN%2FUI-F5F5F5?style=flat-square&labelColor=161B22&logo=shadcnui&logoColor=FFFFFF)](https://ui.shadcn.com) [![Official site](https://img.shields.io/badge/OFFICIAL-SOLID%20GLASS-FFFFFF?style=flat-square&labelColor=161B22&logo=safari&logoColor=FFFFFF)](https://deeplethe.github.io/solid-glass) [![Registry](https://img.shields.io/badge/REGISTRY-13%20ITEMS-8957E5?style=flat-square&labelColor=161B22)](https://deeplethe.github.io/solid-glass/r/registry.json) [![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/TAILWIND%20CSS-4-06B6D4?style=flat-square&labelColor=161B22&logo=tailwindcss&logoColor=FFFFFF)](https://tailwindcss.com) [![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/REACT-19-61DAFB?style=flat-square&labelColor=161B22&logo=react&logoColor=FFFFFF)](https://react.dev) [![Built by DeepLethe](https://img.shields.io/badge/BUILT%20BY-DEEPLETHE-2D333B?style=flat-square&labelColor=161B22)](https://github.com/deeplethe)
A refined glass-inspired aesthetic that feels solid from afar and reveals its subtle materiality up close. Delicate highlights, fine borders, and soft shadows create depth, while a restrained finish emphasizes clarity, stability, and a sense of solidity over transparency, refraction, and fluidity. [![An agent workspace made of it: sessions, the thread, files and background tasks](docs/screenshots/agent-workspace.webp)](https://deeplethe.github.io/solid-glass/blocks) That is one of the [blocks](https://deeplethe.github.io/solid-glass/blocks): whole screens made of the components, to look at, read and copy in. Below, the components themselves. ![The components in the dark theme](docs/screenshots/home-dark-2.webp) ![The components in the light theme](docs/screenshots/home-light-2.webp) It stands between flat design and liquid glass. Flat is an opaque block with no finish to speak of; liquid glass is nearly clear, and on a page with a lot of text the reader is always fighting the background for the words. Solid Glass lets only an outline through: enough to know it is glass, not enough to get in the way of reading. ![One panel three ways: flat, Solid Glass, liquid glass](docs/screenshots/compare.webp) ## The style | | | |---|---| | **Tactility** | Interfaces that feel tangible. Every interaction carries a subtle sense of touch and response. | | **Precision** | Clean geometry, refined details, and restrained lighting create a precise, technical aesthetic. | | **Physicality** | Depth comes from thickness, shadow, and spatial hierarchy, giving every element a sense of physical presence. | | **Materiality** | Subtle edge highlights, fine borders, and soft shadows define the character of each surface. | ### Why it is built this way AI applications are built around information that is constantly changing — responses streaming in, agents performing tasks, and decisions waiting for human input. Solid Glass keeps the interface calm and readable. Neutral surfaces reduce visual distractions, depth establishes hierarchy, and color and motion are reserved for meaningful feedback. The entire system is built with lightweight CSS and works with existing shadcn/ui components in both light and dark modes. The [Material](https://deeplethe.github.io/solid-glass/docs/material) page shows how a pane is made, and the [Create](https://deeplethe.github.io/solid-glass/create) page lets you turn the dials. ## Install Solid Glass is one stylesheet. It finds each part of a shadcn/ui component by the `data-slot` and the classes it already carries, so the components you have need no changes. Start from a shadcn/ui project (React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, the Base UI components): ```bash npx shadcn@latest init ``` Add the stylesheet, straight from this repository: ```bash npx shadcn@latest add deeplethe/solid-glass/solid-glass ``` Import it after Tailwind and shadcn's stylesheet, and delete the `:root` and `.dark` colour variables that `shadcn init` wrote (Solid Glass defines the same names): ```css @import "tailwindcss"; @import "tw-animate-css"; @import "shadcn/tailwind.css"; @import "./solid-glass.css"; ``` Dark is the material as designed; light is there too. The [installation page](https://deeplethe.github.io/solid-glass/docs/installation) has the rest. Solid Glass's own components install the same way: ```bash npx shadcn@latest add deeplethe/solid-glass/status-glyph ``` | Component | What it is | |---|---| | `status-glyph` | Three points of light that say a turn is going, and what it is doing. | | `panel`, `tag`, `dot-loader` | The thinnest pane, a small label, and a row of dots that waits. | | `turn-status`, `composer`, `tool-steps`, `diff-view`, `ask-card`, `context-ring`, `task-notice`, `reasoning` | For interfaces where an agent works: its status line, the box you write to it in, the steps it took, a diff, a question it asks, how full its context is, a notice from a task, and its thinking. | ## What is here | Path | What it is | |---|---| | `src/solid-glass.css` | The theme. The whole material in one file: colours, the three thicknesses of glass, the one state, motion. It defines shadcn/ui's own variable names. | | `registry.json` | The registry: what `shadcn add` installs from. Written by `scripts/build-registry.mjs`, which also builds `public/r/` for the site. | | `src/components/ui/` | The components the site shows. shadcn/ui's (Base UI, `base-nova`), installed with its command line, and Solid Glass's own. A few of shadcn/ui's (`button`, `input`, `tabs`, `dialog`, `dropdown-menu`, `sheet`, `sidebar` and some form controls) differ from stock in small ways; the stylesheet does not depend on those differences. | | `src/create/`, `src/pages/create.tsx` | The Create page: the material with its dials out (thickness, tint, chart colour, type, radius, rim, blur), a preview that takes each choice as it is made, and the few lines of CSS that come of it. `options.ts` says what each choice does to the stylesheet's variables; the preview cards are shadcn/ui's. | | `src/blocks/`, `src/pages/blocks.tsx` | Blocks: whole screens made of the components, shown on the Blocks page in a frame of their own (`/view/`). The single files at the top of the folder are Solid Glass's own (`agent-workspace`) and are in its registry; the folders are shadcn/ui's blocks in the material, installed from shadcn/ui. | | `src/examples/` | One small file per example, as on ui.shadcn.com: shadcn/ui's own examples, and Solid Glass's for its own components. | | `content/` | The documentation. `components/` is shadcn/ui's page for each component; `solid/` and `docs/` are Solid Glass's. | | `src/site/`, `src/pages/`, `src/home/` | The site: header, sidebar, component preview, and the wall of cards on the home page. | | `.github/` | The checks every pull request must pass (`checks.yml`), the workflow that publishes `main` (`pages.yml`), and the templates for issues and pull requests. | | `scripts/build-docs.mjs` | Turns `content/` into `src/docs/generated.json`, which the site renders. | ## Run ```bash npm install npm run dev # http://localhost:5191 npm run build # into dist/ npm run typecheck ``` `/dev/banner` (development only) is the banner above, drawn with the theme: `docs/banner-5.webp` is a screenshot of it in an 820 by 200 window at twice the size, saved as WebP like the other pictures here (a quarter of the size of the same picture as PNG). When the picture changes, save it under the next number and point the README at that: GitHub serves a README's pictures from one address per file, whatever is added to the link, and a browser keeps what it fetched from it. `/dev/examples` (development only) mounts every example at once and lists any that fail. It takes `?q=button,card` to show some of them, `?theme=light`, `?hover=` to show what matches as if the pointer were on it, and `?click=` to press something and look at what it opens. `SOLID_GLASS_ORIGIN` is the address the site is served from (Solid Glass's own components name one another by it) and `SOLID_GLASS_BASE` the path it lives under there; the defaults are this repository's GitHub Pages. ## Add a component of Solid Glass's own 1. `src/components/ui/.tsx`, written like a shadcn/ui component: function components, a `data-slot` on every part, `cn()` from `@/lib/utils`. 2. `src/examples/-demo.tsx`, and one file per further example. 3. `content/solid/.mdx`: front matter (`title`, `description`), then ``, Installation, Usage, and a heading per example. Keep to the four rules (the Material page shows them): the finish is at the edge; heavy, not airy; depth is thickness; one state. ## Contributing Changes land on `dev` by pull request and reach `main`, and with it the published site and registry, when a maintainer merges `dev` into it. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) has the rest ([中文](CONTRIBUTING.zh-CN.md)): what to open an issue for first, what to run before pushing, and what review sends back. How we treat each other is in the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md); security reports go to the address in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Licence [MIT](LICENSE). The components, examples and component documentation that come from shadcn/ui are its authors', also under the MIT License: see [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md).

items.name: BRUTAL
items.description: A free, open source C# framework for making games, or your own game engine. Direct access to native APIs and Vulkan, with the low-level libraries around them. The foundation under Kitten Space Agency and RimWorld's Waylith engine.
items.readme: # BRUTAL Framework **A free, open source C# framework for making games, or your own game engine.** BRUTAL is a framework. You can make a game directly with it, or use it as the foundation for a separate engine. We made Kitten Space Agency directly on BRUTAL. Ludeon built their Waylith engine on it to move RimWorld off Unity. At its core is a custom interop layer giving C# direct access to native APIs and libraries. Around that we've built mathematics, memory management, strings, collections, job scheduling, logging, localization, and bindings for Vulkan, GLFW, Dear ImGui, FMOD, RakNet, Jolt and Box2D. BRUTAL doesn't make the architectural decisions for you. You write your own stack. You can use whatever NuGet packages you want, including third-party ones. It's called BRUTAL for a reason. In some ways it's much harder to use than Unity, Unreal or Godot. In other ways, particularly if you're doing something unusual, it's considerably easier. You actually have to know what you want to do first. ## Why You are only as independent as your tools are. Developers have surrendered an extraordinary amount of control over their work to companies whose interests are not necessarily aligned with their own. We're not suggesting everyone should make their own game engine. We're suggesting every developer should have the option to, without having to spend four years building the foundations first. What that means in practice: - **Free, including for commercial games.** No royalties. We don't want a percentage of your game's revenue. We ask for credit. - **Open source.** The source is here under an MIT-based licence. If one day we stop being accountable to developers, you can fork it and go your own way. - **Deliberately small.** We do a few low-level things well: interop, memory, concurrency, maths, strings, and bindings to native libraries, on the latest C# and Vulkan. We avoid allocations and unnecessary overhead and use unmanaged memory and unsafe code where it makes sense. - **A foundation, like a kernel.** Think of the Linux kernel and something like Ubuntu. It's not an exact comparison, but it gets the idea across. We provide the foundation and you build your own systems on top. ### What BRUTAL is not BRUTAL is not trying to be a general-purpose engine. There is no editor, no scene graph and no renderer, and we're not adding them. We push back on efforts to add more, because adding everything is how the industry ended up with the kind of engines we don't want to use. Pull requests that drift away from a clear purpose will be rejected. ## Projects using BRUTAL | Product | Studio | Engine (if any) | | --- | --- | --- | | [RimWorld](https://store.steampowered.com/app/294100/RimWorld/) | Ludeon Studios | Waylith | | [Kitten Space Agency](https://ahwoo.com/app/100000/kitten-space-agency/) | RocketWerkz | Direct on BRUTAL | | Torpedia | RocketWerkz | Direct on BRUTAL | | Art of the Rail | RocketWerkz | Direct on BRUTAL | | [Gruntz](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ROB5IilenZE) | RocketWerkz | Direct on BRUTAL | | Afterskies | Floating Origin Interactive | Direct on BRUTAL | Ludeon report 2 to 4 times the performance of the Unity build in their own tests, with the vast majority of existing mods still compatible. See their [Steam announcement](https://steamcommunity.com/games/294100/announcements/detail/672882362547178634). Kitten Space Agency is a free pre-alpha spaceflight simulation. It runs a solar system at real scale, and is the first major project built directly on BRUTAL. [Download it on Ahwoo](https://ahwoo.com/app/100000/kitten-space-agency/) and see the technology yourself. ## What is in the box Each top-level folder in this repository is one library, published as a NuGet package. Reference only the ones you need. | Library | What it is | | --- | --- | | `Brutal.Core` | Base types, attributes, platform detection, pointer helpers, Roslyn analyzers | | `Brutal.Interop` | The custom interop layer that gives C# direct access to native APIs | | `Brutal.Memory` | Unmanaged memory management and allocators | | `Brutal.Collections` | Collections that don't allocate | | `Brutal.Strings` | String building and handling without allocation | | `Brutal.Maths`, `Brutal.Numerics` | Vector, matrix and numeric types | | `Brutal.Concurrency` | Job system and threading | | `Brutal.Logging` | Logging | | `Brutal.Localization` | Localization | | `Brutal.Vulkan`, `Brutal.Vulkan.Abstractions`, `Brutal.Vulkan.Vma` | Vulkan bindings, abstractions and the Vulkan Memory Allocator | | `Brutal.OpenGl` | OpenGL bindings | | `Brutal.ShaderC`, `Brutal.Slang` | Shader compilation | | `Brutal.Glfw`, `Brutal.Sdl`, `Brutal.Sdl.Image`, `Brutal.Sdl.Mixer`, `Brutal.Sdl.Ttf` | Windowing and input, with SDL's image, audio mixing and font add-ons | | `Brutal.ImGui`, `Brutal.ImGui.*`, `Brutal.ImPlot` | Dear ImGui and ImPlot bindings, docking branch | | `Brutal.Render.Mesh` | Mesh utilities | | `Brutal.Texture`, `Brutal.Texture.Abstractions`, `Brutal.Ktx`, `Brutal.Gli`, `Brutal.Stb` | Texture loading, KTX and compressed formats, image decoding | | `Brutal.Gltf`, `Brutal.MeshOptimizer` | glTF loading and mesh optimisation | | `Brutal.FreeType` | Font rasterisation | | `Brutal.Fmod`, `Brutal.OpenAl` | Audio | | `Brutal.RakNet` | Networking | | `Brutal.Jolt`, `Brutal.Box2D` | 3D and 2D physics | | `Brutal.Monitor.Common`, `Brutal.Monitor.Host`, `Brutal.RenderDoc`, `Brutal.RenderDoc.ImGui` | Runtime monitoring and RenderDoc capture integration | | `Brutal.NativeFileDialog`, `Brutal.NotCurses`, `Brutal.ZLib` | Native file dialogs, terminal UI, compression | Third-party notices for each library live in its `LICENSES` folder, `Brutal.ImGui/LICENSES` say. ## Getting started ### Prerequisites - [.NET 10 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download) - A Vulkan 1.3 capable GPU with current drivers (if you render) - The [Vulkan SDK](https://vulkan.lunarg.com/) if you want validation layers while developing - Windows or Linux ### Your first window Create a project and add Core and Glfw: ```sh dotnet new console -n HelloBrutal cd HelloBrutal dotnet add package Ahwoo.Brutal.Core dotnet add package Ahwoo.Brutal.Glfw ``` Replace `Program.cs`: ```csharp using Brutal.GlfwApi; using Brutal.Numerics; if (!Glfw.Init()) throw new Exception("Failed to initialize GLFW"); Glfw.WindowHint(GlfwWindowHint.ClientApi, 0); var window = Glfw.CreateWindow(new GlfwWindow.CreateInfo { Title = "Hello BRUTAL", Size = new int2(1280, 720), }); while (!window.ShouldClose) Glfw.PollEvents(); Glfw.Terminate(); ``` ```sh dotnet run ``` That opens a window with no graphics API. What you add next is up to you: - **Rendering:** `Ahwoo.Brutal.Vulkan.Abstractions` and `Ahwoo.Brutal.Vulkan.Vma` for a Vulkan renderer, `Ahwoo.Brutal.ShaderC` to compile shaders at runtime. - **Debug UI:** `Ahwoo.Brutal.ImGui` and `Ahwoo.Brutal.ImPlot`. - **Parallelism:** `Ahwoo.Brutal.Concurrency` for the job system. - **Audio and networking:** `Ahwoo.Brutal.Fmod`, `Ahwoo.Brutal.RakNet`. Questions and "how do I" threads go on the [Guides and Help forum](https://forums.ahwoo.com/forums/brutal/guides-and-help/). ### Building from source This is the source for every published package. Project files, a solution and build scripts are coming. Until then use the NuGet packages, and use this repository to read and fork the code. ```sh git clone https://github.com/ahwootech/BRUTAL.git ``` ## Licence BRUTAL is free to use, modify and distribute, including in commercial games. There are no royalties and we don't want a percentage of your game's revenue. The licence is based on MIT with an added attribution requirement. A game or product built with BRUTAL: 1. includes the BRUTAL copyright notice in its credits screen, or equivalent (section 2.1) 2. shows the BRUTAL logo before gameplay starts (section 2.2) 3. ships `NOTICE.txt` alongside the product (section 2.3) If you don't want to do that, we can arrange a separate commercial licence. We also waive the logo requirement for non-profit projects and where displaying it would be detrimental to the application's purpose. BRUTAL is open source. There are already OSI-approved licences that allow graphical attribution. Ours is not yet OSI approved because we have not submitted it yet. We intend to, and to develop the licence with community feedback. See [LICENSE.txt](LICENSE.txt) for the full text. Third-party components keep their own licences. Section 4.0 points at the `LICENSES` folder at the root of each NuGet package; in this repository, those notices are in the `LICENSES` folder of each library that redistributes them. ## Contributing You can submit PRs and issues. We are a small team and maintaining a public framework is going to be a lot of work, so please be patient with us. We'll see what happens, assess the problems, and change our workflows as necessary. What won't change is BRUTAL's scope. Before opening a PR, read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). It covers scope, what we expect from AI-assisted contributions, the contribution grant in section 5.0 of the licence, and the sign-off every commit needs. Small changes you understand and have tested, with a clear purpose, are the ones that will get merged. - Security issues: report them privately, see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). Don't open a public issue. - Conduct: [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). ## Community - Source: https://github.com/ahwootech/BRUTAL - NuGet packages: https://www.nuget.org/profiles/Ahwoo - Forums: https://forums.ahwoo.com/forums/brutal/ - Discord: https://discord.gg/MEuNTYbAh8 ## Credits BRUTAL was made by the RocketWerkz Enterprise team and others, named in [CONTRIBUTORS.md](CONTRIBUTORS.md). When we talk about wanting credit for BRUTAL, these are the people we are talking about. BRUTAL is Copyright (c) 2024 Ahwoo Limited.

items.name: handwired
items.description: Turn your regular JavaScript code into a neural net.
items.readme:
# Handwired

Turn your regular JavaScript code into a neural net; no training, exact, yet also fully differentiable!

## How It Works

A program's made of if-else, loops, and state. Handwired transforms them into matrix multiplication + reglu over floats. For example:

```ts
const a = 5
const result = (a > 4) ? 10 : 12
```

The above can be expressed as basic arithmetic:

```ts
const a = 5
// Math.max(0, x) is ReLU. For an integer a, above4 is 1 if a > 4, and 0 otherwise
const above4 = Math.max(0, a - 4) - Math.max(0, a - 5)
// Both branches compute, and above4 picks one
const result = above4 * 10 + (1 - above4) * 12
```

You can calculate that by hand and see that both arrive at the same result.

We then collect the + and * and relu into a giant matmul, and either run it on JS or WebGPU, for fun.

Because we basically only use these 2 primitives:
- the full program stays differentiable
- the weights don't need training since they're written manually
- existing gpu techniques, such as fusion, sparsity, reordering, have a great time optimizing such minimal primitives

This unlocks lots of funny use-cases, like:
- unfreezing the weights and train them (what does that even do? Let's find out!)
- attaching a specific frozen program to a generic neural net and train end-to-end (now a nanoGPT can do both Shakespeare and your particular UI?)
- achieving GPU-level of parallelism with JS code that was written in a traditional single-threaded way (see the JSON search demo that runs in milliseconds over 100k documents)

## Play With It

Try the demos live: https://chenglou.me/handwired/

`git clone && bun install`, then `bun start` to run them locally. Check `docs/`, `src/` and `template/` to get started! (`lab/` is a bunch of old experiments you can check or ignore)

![HandwiredOS](assets/demos-handwiredos.webp)

items.readme:
Git designed for AI agents.

Anthropic built **Scion**, a faster version control system for coding agents, and described it in [Redesigning source control](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/redesigning-source-control): a server-centric system built for hundreds of agents that read, write and land code at the same time. Scion is internal to Anthropic and is not available to the public. So I built **gitai**: an open-source version of that design that anyone can run, and that the community can improve and maintain together. MIT licensed. Vendor neutral: the server never calls a language model, and every AI feature works with any provider, or none. gitai is an independent implementation of the publicly described design. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic. --- ## Why Classic Git hosting was built for humans who clone a repository, work for hours and push once. Coding agents work differently: thousands of short-lived tasks, each touching a few files, each wanting to land in seconds, all on the same branches. Full clones, merge queues and client-side history walks become the bottleneck. Scion's answer is to move the work to the server: clients stay online and fetch only what they need, history questions are answered (and cached) by the server, changes land through a compare-and-swap instead of a queue, every update is an entry in a changeset log, and the repository state lives in a consistent database plus object storage so servers scale out. gitai implements these ideas, with normal Git repositories underneath. ## The Scion ideas, implemented | Scion idea | In gitai | |---|---| | **Always-online clients** that fetch exactly what they need | `ObjectService` serves single objects and sparse trees; `graft clone` and `graft sparse` materialize only the paths you ask for. | | **Source control as an API**: history runs on the server | Blame, path history, ancestry and code search run server-side and are memoized as derived data, computed once per commit. | | **Landing without a merge queue** | `UserLand` rebases a change onto the current tip and lands it with a compare-and-swap; concurrent lands on one branch are batched into a single reference update. | | **Automatic conflict resolution** | A conflicting land is resolved by a resolver you choose (any LLM provider, a deterministic tool, or none) through a versioned, vendor-neutral protocol. | | **Changeset log** | Every accepted reference update is recorded with its operation and actor in a dense, ordered log that clients list or watch live. | | **Storage core: a database and object storage, stateless servers** | Each change is a changeset in a write-ahead log in SQLite or PostgreSQL, with a compare-and-swap per reference; packs live in object storage (file, S3, GCS, Azure). Server nodes are caches that any node can rebuild, so you add nodes to scale. | | **Test after landing, revert the culprit** | `graft-verify` tests the tip, bisects a failure and reverts the change that broke it. | | **Monitoring agents ("superfans")** | Agents follow the changeset stream and report what matters to each component, also through Slack. | | **Agent-friendly review** | Reviews with semantic approval rules: a comment-only change can need fewer approvals than a logic change. | | **Agents as first-class users** | Per-agent tokens, an RPC allowlist and branch policies decide what each agent may do. | | **Strict cache tiers** | `graft-cache` caches immutable objects in daemon and regional tiers, verifying every object. | ## Architecture ``` agents, CI jobs, sparse workspaces graft CLI / Go SDK | v gRPC +-------------------------------------------------+ | graft-cache (optional daemon and cache tiers) | +------------------------+------------------------+ v +---------------------------------------------------------------+ | gitai server (any number of nodes) | | land - objects - changesets - derived data - search - review | | write path: changeset + compare-and-swap per reference | +-----------+--------------------------------+------------------+ | | v v +-----------------------+ +-----------------------------+ | SQLite / PostgreSQL | | object storage | | changeset WAL, refs, | | content-addressed packs | | changelog, reviews | | (file, S3, GCS, Azure) | +-----------------------+ +-----------------------------+ \ / local Git repositories = caches any node can rebuild ``` Details: [ARCHITECTURE.md](doc/graft/ARCHITECTURE.md) and [STORAGE.md](doc/graft/STORAGE.md). ## Quick start Requirements: Linux or macOS, Go 1.26, a C toolchain, Meson and Ninja (the build compiles a bundled Git). ```shell git clone https://github.com/feder-cr/git-ai.git cd git-ai make build # server, CLI and tools into _build/bin examples/graft/quickstart.sh # a server, a cache daemon, two agents and a land, in a temporary directory ./_build/bin/graft # the CLI and its commands ``` To run your own server, adapt [`examples/graft/config.toml`](examples/graft/config.toml) and start it with `_build/bin/gitaly serve config.toml`. To put the repository state in a database and object storage, add a `[graft.storage]` section: start in `shadow` mode, import your repositories, then switch to `authoritative` ([STORAGE.md](doc/graft/STORAGE.md)). Inside the code the extensions are called **Graft**: the `[graft]` configuration section, the `graft` CLI, `internal/graft` and `doc/graft`. ## Documentation - [Quickstart](doc/graft/QUICKSTART.md) and [configuration reference](doc/graft/CONFIGURATION.md) - [Architecture](doc/graft/ARCHITECTURE.md) and the [storage core](doc/graft/STORAGE.md) - [Landing and batching](doc/graft/LAND-BATCHING.md), [conflict resolution](doc/graft/RESOLVE.md), [derived data](doc/graft/DERIVED.md) - [Review](doc/graft/REVIEW.md), [search](doc/graft/SEARCH.md), [verification](doc/graft/VERIFY.md), [superfans](doc/graft/SUPERFAN.md) and [Slack chat](doc/graft/SUPERFAN-CHAT.md) - [Agent security](doc/graft/AGENT-SECURITY.md), [benchmarks](doc/graft/BENCH.md), [fuzzing](doc/graft/FUZZING.md) - [Limitations and roadmap](doc/graft/LIMITATIONS.md) - Design documents of each phase: [PLAN.md](doc/graft/PLAN.md) to [PLAN6.md](doc/graft/PLAN6.md) ## Status Version 0.1.0, the first public release. Everything above is implemented and covered by unit, end-to-end, multi-node, crash and fuzz tests. Interfaces may still change before 1.0. Known gaps (for example garbage collection of packs in the storage core) are listed in [LIMITATIONS.md](doc/graft/LIMITATIONS.md). ## Community gitai is meant to be maintained by its community. Open an issue to report a bug or propose an idea, start a discussion before a large design change, and send pull requests: tests and a short description of the reasoning make them easy to review. The design documents in `doc/graft/PLAN*.md` explain why things are the way they are. ## Credits and license gitai is MIT licensed, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). It started as a fork of [Gitaly](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitaly), GitLab's Git RPC server (MIT, Copyright GitLab Inc.), which provides the Git plumbing underneath; every upstream Gitaly RPC keeps working. The non-MIT `ee/` directory of upstream Gitaly is not part of this repository. Gitaly's own README is kept in [doc/UPSTREAM-GITALY.md](doc/upstream/README-GITALY.md), and third-party notices are in [NOTICE](NOTICE).

items.description: Your TV, minus the ads. Debloat any Android TV over ADB and give it a clean, tvOS-inspired launcher. Built in an afternoon with Claude Code.
items.readme:
# tv-vibehack **Your TV, minus the ads.** Strip the bloatware from any Android TV or Google TV over Wi-Fi, and replace the ad-filled home screen with a clean launcher that looks like an Apple TV. No root, no cable, nothing uninstalled, and a one-line restore if you change your mind. ![Before: stock Google TV home with a sponsored ad. After: the tv-vibehack launcher](docs/stock-vs-new-side.jpg) It started as an afternoon fixing my parents' Mi TV, which showed them an advert before they could reach Netflix. The whole thing was done with Claude Code talking to the real TV, and the prompt that did it is in this repo so you can do the same with yours. --- ## Table of contents - [How it works](#how-it-works) - [Quick start](#quick-start) - [What you get](#what-you-get) - [Supported TVs](#supported-tvs) - [Doing it by hand](#doing-it-by-hand) - [The launcher](#the-launcher) - [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) - [Questions people ask](#questions-people-ask) - [Contributing](#contributing) - [Licence](#licence) --- ## How it works Android TVs have the same debug bridge as Android phones. Once you switch on USB debugging in the TV's developer options, the TV listens on your Wi-Fi and asks you once to allow your computer. After that, everything is standard Android tooling: 1. **Back up** the list of installed packages and settings. 2. **Disable** the manufacturer's telemetry, ad services, content rows and preloaded junk with `pm disable-user`. Nothing is uninstalled, so a restore script can undo every step. 3. **Install** a small native launcher and make it the default home screen. The bloat differs by brand, which is why the prompt asks your coding assistant to discover it on your TV and ask you before touching anything you might use. ## Quick start You need a computer on the same Wi-Fi as the TV and a coding assistant with shell access (Claude Code, or anything similar). **1. On the TV** Settings → Device Preferences → About → press OK on **Build** seven times → go back → Developer options → turn on **USB debugging**. Some TVs also show a Network or ADB debugging toggle; turn it on too. Keep the TV switched on. **2. On your computer** Open your assistant, paste the prompt from [`PROMPT.md`](PROMPT.md), and fill in your TV model. **3. Follow along** Accept the "Allow USB debugging?" prompt when it appears on the TV, then answer the checklist questions: which streaming apps you use, which four go in the dock, whether to keep the voice assistant, Chromecast and firmware updates. That's it. The assistant backs up, debloats, builds and installs the launcher, and checks every step with screenshots pulled from the TV. On a 1 GB Mi TV the whole thing took one afternoon the first time; with this repo as context, people report about fifteen minutes. ## What you get A home screen that is yours again: - **Pitch-black background** and a dock of your four favourite apps at the bottom, in a lighter rounded band, exactly where Apple TV puts it. - **A top shelf** showing the focused app's name in large type, with an ambient glow in a colour taken from the app's own artwork. - **The rest of your apps in a grid** that slides up when you press Down. - **One floating glass highlight** that springs from tile to tile instead of each tile drawing its own border. The focused tile lifts slightly and shows its name. - **Three frosted buttons**: Inputs (a dropdown of HDMI ports, AV and Live TV), Wi-Fi (showing the network you're on) and Settings. - **A greeting, a large thin clock and the date**, set in [Outfit](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Outfit). - **A matching Clock screensaver**, optional, that drifts around the screen so nothing burns in. And a TV that stops working against you: no sponsored rows, no "Discover" nags, no analytics phoning home, no apps you never asked for. ## Supported TVs Anything running **Android TV** or **Google TV**: Xiaomi and Redmi, TCL, Hisense, Sony, OnePlus, Realme, Nvidia Shield and most others. Not supported: Samsung (Tizen), LG (webOS) and Amazon Fire TV. They run different systems or won't let a third-party launcher take over Home. Lists that people have tested and contributed live in [`examples/`](examples/): | TV | OS | |---|---| | Xiaomi Mi TV 4A (MiTV-MOOQ1) | Android TV 10 | | Xiaomi MiTV-AXSO0 | Android TV 9 | | TCL 55" 4K Google TV, 2023 (G10) | Google TV 12 | | SANYO ATV R2 | Android TV 9 | | OnePlus TV (D00) | Google TV 14 | Your TV not here? The prompt works regardless, it discovers the bloat itself. If you add your list afterwards, the next person with your model skips that step. See [Contributing](#contributing). ## Doing it by hand Everything the assistant does, you can run yourself. The tools need Python 3 and nothing else. ```bash python3 -m venv tools/venv && tools/venv/bin/pip install -r tools/requirements.txt export TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 # your TV's IP address tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/tv.py --probe # model, Android version, firmware tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/tv.py 'pm list packages' # run one shell command on the TV printf 'cmd1\ncmd2\n' | tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/tv.py --batch # several, one connection tools/disable.sh examples/xiaomi-mi-tv-4a/debloat.txt # apply a debloat list tools/restore.sh examples/xiaomi-mi-tv-4a/debloat.txt # undo it and restore the stock launcher ``` | Tool | What it does | |---|---| | [`tools/tv.py`](tools/tv.py) | A pure-Python ADB client: shell, batch, push, pull. Works where the stock `adb` binary is blocked. | | [`tools/b64push.py`](tools/b64push.py) | Uploads larger files such as APKs as base64 chunks and verifies the checksum. | | [`tools/disable.sh`](tools/disable.sh) / [`tools/restore.sh`](tools/restore.sh) | Apply or undo a debloat list. PowerShell versions sit next to them. | ### Windows The PowerShell scripts work without WSL or Git Bash. With Android Studio installed nothing else is needed: the install script uses Android Studio's bundled JDK and the default SDK location. ```powershell python -m venv tools\venv; tools\venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r tools\requirements.txt powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File launcher\build-and-install.ps1 -TvHost 192.168.1.50 powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\disable.ps1 -TvHost 192.168.1.50 examples\xiaomi-mi-tv-4a\debloat.txt powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\restore.ps1 -TvHost 192.168.1.50 examples\xiaomi-mi-tv-4a\debloat.txt ``` The install script stops before touching the stock launcher if the install or the home-screen switch fails. Git Bash also works; the `.sh` scripts detect a Windows venv and disable MSYS path rewriting themselves. ## The launcher A small native Android TV app (`com.gathin.tvhome`, about 1.6 MB), written in plain Java with AndroidX RecyclerView and nothing heavier. It is built for sets with 1 GB of RAM: no blur, no video, no network, no background services. **Configure** it in [`launcher/app/src/main/res/values/config.xml`](launcher/app/src/main/res/values/config.xml): the dock order, apps to hide, your TV's Live TV package, and the number of columns. **Build and install** with one command: ```bash TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 launcher/build-and-install.sh ``` It needs JDK 17 and the Android SDK (platform 34, build-tools 34.0.0). On macOS: ```bash brew install openjdk@17 android-commandlinetools sdkmanager "platforms;android-34" "build-tools;34.0.0" ``` Without Homebrew, the script also finds a JDK 17 known to `/usr/libexec/java_home` and an SDK in `~/Library/Android/sdk`, Android Studio's default. A release build (`./gradlew assembleRelease`) is smaller and faster on 1 GB sets; sign it yourself before installing. **Navigation** is deliberate: Up and Down move exactly one row, Up from the dock goes to the top buttons, the ends of the button row don't fall through to tiles, and the last focused app is remembered when you come back, even after the app list changes.
Optional: the Clock screensaver A large thin clock and the date over an ambient glow, in the launcher's style. Every minute the clock drifts to a new spot and the glow shifts colour. The system runs it only while the TV is idle. Turn it on over ADB, or pick "Clock" in the TV's screensaver settings: ```bash tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/tv.py 'settings put secure screensaver_components com.gathin.tvhome/.ClockDream; settings put secure screensaver_enabled 1' ``` It starts after the TV's "screen off" idle time (`settings get system screen_off_timeout`).
## Troubleshooting Things that bit us or contributors, so they don't bite you. **Connecting** - **macOS: `adb connect` says "No route to host"** although the port is open. Recent macOS treats the Google-signed `adb` as its own app under Local Network privacy and silently blocks it. `tools/tv.py` avoids the binary entirely. - **No "wireless debugging" toggle** on some TVs, Xiaomi among them. USB debugging alone opens network ADB on port 5555. - **Windows PowerShell 5.1 adds a byte-order mark** to text piped into a program, which turned the first batch command into gibberish. `tv.py` now strips it, and the `.ps1` scripts pipe clean UTF-8. - **Git Bash rewrites paths** like `/data/local/tmp` into Windows paths. The scripts set `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` for you. Set `JAVA_HOME` and `ANDROID_HOME` before building there. **Working on the TV** - **Chained `pm` commands** (`pm disable a; pm disable b`) may silently stop after the first. Run one per shell call; `--batch` does exactly that. - **Large pushes hang** through the Python client. Use `tools/b64push.py` for APKs. - **Screenshots come out empty** while Live TV or an HDMI input is on screen, seen on TCL. Press Home before `screencap`. - **Disable the stock launcher only after the new one is installed**, or the Home button lands on a factory test app. - **No on-screen keyboard** after switching launchers, seen on Xiaomi: the default input method pointed at a Baidu keyboard that isn't installed. Fix: `tools/tv.py 'ime set com.google.android.inputmethod.latin/com.android.inputmethod.latin.LatinIME'` - **Third-party launchers** often charge for basics like a custom wallpaper. That's why this repo has its own. ## Questions people ask **Is this safe? Can it brick the TV?** No. Nothing is flashed, rooted or deleted. Packages are disabled for the user profile, which lives in the data partition, not in the system image. The firmware is untouched. If something goes wrong, `tools/restore.sh` puts everything back, and even without the tools you can re-enable apps from the TV's own settings. **What about firmware updates?** Most lists disable the manufacturer's update service, so updates only arrive when you re-enable it on purpose. If an update does land, the worst case is that a package comes back enabled and you re-run the script. **Won't the apps break as their APIs change?** The streaming apps still update through the Play Store, which is left alone. The launcher doesn't talk to them; it lists what's installed and launches it, using Android launcher intents that have been stable for over a decade. **How did it get access? Isn't that a security hole?** Through the Android Debug Bridge, with one explicit "allow this computer" tap on the TV, the same as developing an Android app. The TV only trusts the key you approved. You can switch USB debugging off again afterwards and the launcher keeps working. **Can I just download the launcher APK?** Build it yourself with the one-line script above; it takes about a minute and you control what goes on your TV. We don't publish prebuilt binaries. ## Contributing The most useful contribution is your TV's debloat list, so the next person with that model doesn't have to rediscover it. Launcher improvements and sharper prompt wording are welcome too. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the format and the testing we ask for. ## Licence MIT, see [`LICENSE`](LICENSE). The Outfit typeface is under the SIL Open Font License, see `launcher/FONT-LICENSE-OFL.txt`.

# Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection for Windows

**Uncharted 1, 2 and 3 from the PS4 collection running natively on Windows 10 and 11, by [SuperMedo](https://github.com/Supermedo).** Mohammed Albarghouthi

Same idea as my [Bloodborne port](https://github.com/Supermedo/bloodborne_pc): the original PS4 game
code runs directly on your PC and the graphics are translated to Vulkan. Unpack the zip, start
`Uncharted.exe`, pick your game folder, choose a game and press **PLAY**.

**[Download the latest version](https://github.com/Supermedo/uncharted_pc/releases/latest)** · **[Join the Discord]([https://discord.gg/yTMG8c4Bqm](https://discord.gg/s3RgH6cRfJ))**

> **No game files are included.** You need your own decrypted dump of the collection
> (CUSA02343, CUSA02320, ...: the folder with eboot.bin, big2-ps4_Shipping.elf,
> big3-ps4_Shipping.elf, sce_sys, u1data, u2data and u3data).
> This project is not affiliated with Sony Interactive Entertainment or Naughty Dog.

## Features

- All three games from one launcher: Drake's Fortune, Among Thieves and Drake's Deception.
- 60 FPS like on PS4, or 120 FPS (higher rates are experimental).
- Anti-aliasing with TAA, AMD FSR 3.1, AMD FSR 4 or NVIDIA DLSS (DLAA).
- Frame generation: AMD FSR 3 (any GPU) or NVIDIA DLSS (RTX 40 2x, RTX 50 up to 4x).
- Keyboard, mouse and controller together, all remappable. Mouse look in U3.
- Add to Steam and desktop shortcuts from the launcher, automatic updates.

## Requirements

- Windows 10 (1903 or later) or Windows 11, 64-bit.
- A graphics card with Vulkan 1.3 and a current driver.
- About 8 GB of free memory (RAM + page file).

## Known problems

- **Uncharted 3, Cartagena square (chapter 2):** at high frame rates (240 Hz setting, ~80 FPS)
  the game could freeze and close with "GPU crash: the graphics device was lost". It came from
  the speed fix for that area and is fixed in 0.3. If it still happens to you, set Frame rate to
  60 on the Display page and open an issue with your `user\last_run.log`.
- **Uncharted 3:** green or black shapes flash for a single frame on some characters (Sully's
  shirt in Cartagena). It happens in shadPS4 too, so it's a shader translation problem. Not fixed yet.
- **Crash with "ASSERTION: GetRenderFrameParams(frameToFreeInstancesFor)->m_gfxEopTick":** the
  game got too many frames ahead of the GPU side while it was busy (building shaders on a first
  run). 0.3.1 holds the game at most one frame ahead, like on PS4. If you still see it, open an
  issue with your log.
- Frame rates above 120 are experimental.

## Building

MSYS2 CLANG64 on Windows: `bash build.sh` builds `out\bb-probe.exe`, and
`bash packaging/windows/package.sh` makes `dist\uncharted-windows` and the zip.

## Credits

Built on [bbport](https://github.com/deadinside28/bloodborne_pc), the native Linux port of
Bloodborne by deadinside28, and on the [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4)
renderer. Video decoding (Videodec2) and the DLSS bridge come from
[IFreemz/shadPS4-Bloodborne-DLSS-FSR](https://github.com/IFreemz/shadPS4-Bloodborne-DLSS-FSR).
Thanks to Mindro for the shadPS4 Uncharted build that showed which problems to look for.

Also used: [FSR-Vulkan](https://github.com/FireBurn/FSR-Vulkan) and the AMD FidelityFX SDK (FSR),
FSR 4 assets from [FireBurn/Q2RTX](https://github.com/FireBurn/Q2RTX), the
[NVIDIA DLSS SDK](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS) (`nvngx_dlss.dll` under NVIDIA's license),
[LibAtrac9](https://github.com/Thealexbarney/LibAtrac9), [SDL3](https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL),
[FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org), [Dear ImGui](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui),
[sirit](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/sirit), [magic_enum](https://github.com/Neargye/magic_enum),
[xbyak](https://github.com/herumi/xbyak),
[Vulkan Memory Allocator](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/VulkanMemoryAllocator),
[MSYS2](https://www.msys2.org) / [LLVM](https://llvm.org), [PyInstaller](https://pyinstaller.org),
[Pillow](https://python-pillow.org) and the Cinzel font (SIL Open Font License).

NVIDIA, GeForce RTX and DLSS are trademarks of NVIDIA Corporation. The default covers and the
icon are original artwork; no official art is included.

## License

GNU GPL v2 or later ([LICENSE](LICENSE)). Third-party components keep their own licenses
(see `licenses\` in the download).

# Open Claude UI (`open-claude-ui`)

基于 REA 深度拆解，高保真生产级还原 Claude 设计系统 (CDS) 与工程交互物理学。

简体中文 · English

--- ## 📖 简介 (Introduction) `open-claude-ui` 是基于对现代桌面端 AI 客户端进行深度拆解与逆向分析构建的高保真开源 UI 组件库与动效引擎。 整个逆向推导、反混淆静态分析与 ASAR 资源解构，均依托于先进的多平台逆向工程框架 **[REA (Reverse Engineer Anything)](https://github.com/morluto/rea)** 完成——通过 REA 的静态 AST 解析、闭包代码反混淆与运行时跟踪能力，穿透生产级压缩包，精准还原了底层工程物理常数与数学模型。 不同于市面上常见的盲猜或近似复刻，本项目所有组件规范、物理阻尼常数、着色器关键帧及音频管道均**严格依据真实前端架构反编译验证**提炼而成： * **温润的人文质感 (Editorial Warmth)**：纯正陶土橙（Clay `#d97757`）、4 层微对比表面阶梯（Surface 0-3）与视网膜高分屏发丝细边补偿（Hairline Ring）； * **严苛的交互物理学 (Interaction Physics)**：4 套生产级物理弹簧参数调校、4px 指针移动死区、CJK 输入法合成守卫、7 档渐隐非线性 Alpha 遮罩； * **高阶视听与系统架构 (Audiovisual & Architecture)**：基于原生 Web Audio API 的零延迟合成提示音、以光标为锚点的画廊跑道平移缩放、macOS 桌面毛玻璃透明融合与 Cowork 多代理协同拓扑。 > ⚖️ **版权与合规声明 (DMCA & Assets Policy)**： > 本开源项目**不公开分发任何专有二进制资产**（包括商业字体 `.ttf` 与录音 `.mp3`）。本项目提供原生系统级字体回退栈与 Web Audio API 纯代码合成音效，完全自包含、合规安全。详情参见 [assets/README.md](assets/README.md)。 --- ## 🌟 核心特性 (Key Features) ```mermaid graph TD OCUI["open-claude-ui"] OCUI --> Tokens["1. 设计哲学与令牌体系
(Surfaces 0-3, Clay, Hairlines, System Fonts)"] OCUI --> Atoms["2. 基础原子交互控件
(CdsButton, SegmentedControl, StatusIndicators, Dialog)"] OCUI --> Stream["3. 会话流与指令引擎
(Composer, IME Guard, Model Switcher, MCP Cards)"] OCUI --> Motion["4. 动效物理学与着色器
(Spring Physics, Ambient Shimmer, Scroll Fade Masks)"] OCUI --> Media["5. 视听多媒体与产物交互
(Synthetic Audio, Lightbox Pan/Zoom, Split Resizer, Epitaxy)"] OCUI --> Desktop["6. 桌面架构与协作拓扑
(macOS Vibrancy, Sidebar DnD, Cowork Canvas, A11y Roving)"] OCUI --> Setup["7. 完整工程规范与开箱即用
